title: Convert float strings such as "10.9" to integer types
provenance: Evaluator-authored problem-only adaptation of upstream PR spf13/cast#261, retrieved 2026-11-24. Written from the change itself; solution text omitted.
body: cast converts the string "10.0" to the integer 10, but returns an error for a string with a nonzero fraction such as "10.9", "-2.5" or "3.", and for a json.Number such as "7.9". Support them: the integer conversions (ToInt, ToInt8 to ToInt64, ToUint, ToUint8 to ToUint64 and their E variants) must convert a decimal string or json.Number by dropping its fractional part, truncating toward zero ("10.9" is 10, "-2.5" is -2). Whole numbers, hexadecimal strings, the empty string and strings that are not numbers must convert exactly as before. ToTime and ToTimeE must keep their current behavior for a json.Number: a whole number such as "1700000000.0" is still a Unix time, and one with a fraction such as "7.9" is still an error. Add tests.
